ranking.rationale: Exact craft match: compact-to-deployed rigid transformation, one legible control, synchronized members, explicit endpoints, collision clearances, capture, and reset are Vela Bloom's central method.
Excellent constraint match for a three-part, support-free, one-action desk mechanism, but less specifically focused than Vela Bloom on a large symbolic unfurling transformation.
Strong at Wish-specific kinetic machines and synchronized motion, though this small serene transformation needs less exposed machinery and mechanical theater than Bob normally favors.
Strong match for a compact two- or three-part reveal with robust tactile handling, but her puzzle/interlock emphasis is secondary to the Wish's synchronized deployment.
Celestial negative space and one-motion reveal fit the star apertures, but light and optical transformation are optional here while rigid wing kinematics are mandatory.
Could make the moth silhouette compelling under light, but the Wish asks for the physical moth silhouette itself rather than a projected second story.
Captive motion and inspectable continuous paths are relevant, but there is no topology-driven runner, braid, or crossing at the center of the Wish.
Would specify linkage truthfully, but the Wish seeks magical kinetic delight rather than a scientific or mathematical phenomenon the owner can test.
Negative space and flat support-free shapes suit the starry wing graphics, but this is a single mechanism rather than a modular arrangement or pattern system.
Hand energy and repeated motion are relevant, but the Wish contains no acoustic behavior and should not acquire sound as an extra premise.
The moth silhouette could become a small world, but the Wish provides no personal subject references and explicitly centers mechanism rather than a recognizable personal scene.
The product is not an original tabletop game and has no rules, strategic roles, or intended player group requiring simulation.
The Wish is neither a known tabletop classic nor a request to preserve existing rules through personalized physical design.
The Wish is a kinetic desk toy, not an abstract strategy game whose depth comes from board structure and combinatorial play.

concept.title: Moon-Moth Bloom — Starplug Crescent
concept.summary: A palm-size crescent chassis and two captured rigid wings form exactly three printed parts. Closed, both wings lie within a backed crescent face while fixed moon-skin bridges cover their tiny star cutouts, reading as a smooth moon pebble. A broad shoe integral to the left wing root slides 21.5 mm along a guarded crescent track; equal meshing root gears rotate both wings 82 degrees in opposite directions, uncovering the stars and expanding into a 136 mm moth silhouette. Sliding the same shoe back positively gears both wings shut.
concept.object_and_category: A one-handed, hand-powered transforming desk toy: a rounded crescent pebble that becomes a planar moon-moth silhouette through a single reversible arcuate thumb-slide.
concept.signature_decision: Use the visible thumb slider as an arcuate control surface integral to one of the two wing parts. It is still one broad sliding gesture, but it avoids a fourth physical part; identical guarded root gears give deterministic equal-and-opposite wing motion. The chassis is the third part and provides both the stable reference and non-flexing bayonet capture.
concept.intended_interaction: Rest the closed crescent across the fingers with the thumb in its concave notch. Push the 20 by 11 mm pad along the engraved crescent track until the open hard stop: the left root drives the identical right root 1:1, so both wings sweep outward together and the six previously masked star apertures become open negative space. Keep fingers on the raised rear grip island, outside the marked lateral sweep. Push the same pad back to the closed stop; no shaking, separate reset, spring, or forced flexing is intended.
concept.wall_and_edge_plan: Nominal wing webs and root-gear faces are 3.0 mm axially; wing perimeter and aperture ligaments are at least 2.4 mm; each stop shoulder is at least 4.8 by 6.0 mm in plan; pivot journals are 5.0 mm diameter; chassis floor is 4.0 mm and guarded root walls are 2.4 mm. Exterior touch edges use at least 2.0 mm radii, crescent tips use 4-7 mm radii, and support-facing transitions use 45 degree chamfers rather than downward fillets.

components.name: Crescent pebble chassis
components.purpose: Provides the smooth palm-size resting form, fixed pivot geometry, gear and finger guards, endpoint stops, closed-state backing and moon-skin bridges, grip island, and assembly capture for both wings.
components.form: A 78 by 54 mm low crescent plate with a broad smooth back, 4.0 mm floor, raised rounded perimeter, two vertical journals, a guarded common-plane gear tunnel, a 15 mm-radius concave thumb-track opening, two 8 mm-long overlapping wing-entry lips, and six local fixed moon-skin bridges. In the closed state each star lies over solid backing and beneath a bridge with 0.50 mm vertical running clearance, so the aperture is not finger-accessible and the front reads as continuous pebble skin.
components.placement: Front view is XY and pivot axes are parallel to Z. Pivot centers are nominally X=+/-9.0 mm and Y=-7.5 mm, 18 mm apart. The lower 24 mm of the convex rim is a fixed grip zone separated from both swept wing exits.
components.interfaces: Each 5.0 mm journal ends in a 7.4 mm-diameter, 1.2 mm-high 45-degree mushroom flange and runs in a distinct 5.6 mm wing bearing bore for 0.30 mm radial clearance per side. A separate 7.8 mm service lobe and 6.0 mm connecting throat admit the flange only at a mirrored 118-degree out-of-range service angle. At that azimuth an open roof gate and a 1.2 mm-high service shelf hold the root above the operating stops; at closed alignment both roots descend together into pockets with 0.45 mm total axial running clearance. Roofs and guide cheeks in the operating range then prevent renewed lift or translation. Operational stops restrict travel to 0-82 degrees, at least 30 degrees from either release corridor. Two complete module-1.0, 18-tooth root gears have 9.0 mm pitch radii and 18 mm center spacing. Guards cover tooth tips and root shear lines while leaving the broad shoe exposed.

components.name: Left moon-moth wing with integral thumb slider
components.purpose: Forms the left half of the closed pebble face, the left deployed moth wing, and the only user control; its complete root gear directly drives the right wing.
components.form: A 3.0 mm rigid swept wing web with a 3.0 mm-axial circular root carrying a complete rounded module-1.0, 18-tooth, 9.0 mm pitch-radius gear, a keyed bearing aperture comprising a 5.6 mm running bore, 7.8 mm service lobe, and 6.0 mm connecting throat, three five-point through-stars measuring 5.5, 6.5, and 7.0 mm across their outer points with 0.5 mm internal corner radii, two shallow vein ribs, and an 18 by 12 by 2.2 mm rounded thumb shoe joined to the root by a 6 mm-wide load path. The outer perimeter is a crescent forewing with a rounded tip, never a sharp point.
components.placement: On the left journal in closed state and entirely inside the 78 by 54 mm chassis projection. It rotates +82 degrees about Z into the left deployed half. The thumb shoe follows a 15 mm-radius, 82-degree arcuate window for 21.5 mm nominal travel.
components.interfaces: Its service lobe passes over the chassis mushroom flange only at +118 degrees and rests 1.2 mm above the operating plane while the second wing is loaded. The two complete root gears mesh in this raised common plane and counter-rotate together to closed alignment; the roots then descend together into the operating pockets. In that plane its gear meshes with the equal right gear with nominal 0.40 mm total flank backlash and 0.25 mm tip relief, values Make must expose as parameters. A broad root stop face contacts chassis pads at 0 and 82 degrees; teeth are not travel stops. Each star passes between solid chassis backing and a fixed moon-skin bridge only at the closed endpoint.

components.name: Right moon-moth driven wing
components.purpose: Completes the closed pebble face and mirrors the left deployed silhouette while remaining positively synchronized and captive.
components.form: A mirror wing web and root matching the left wing's structural thickness, complete 18-tooth root gear, keyed bearing aperture, rounded perimeter, three star apertures, and vein ribs, but without the thumb-shoe arm. A shallow crescent relief replaces the control area so the two closed halves remain visually balanced.
components.placement: On the right journal in closed state and entirely inside the 78 by 54 mm chassis projection. Direct external-gear contact rotates it -82 degrees about Z into the right deployed half as the left wing moves +82 degrees.
components.interfaces: Its mirrored service lobe passes over the chassis flange only at -118 degrees and rests on the same 1.2 mm-high service plane as the left root. The two complete root gears mesh before either root enters the operating pockets; their equal gears are the sole synchronization link during the paired rotation to closed. Mirrored stop shoulders meet the chassis simultaneously within a 0.3 mm nominal timing target after both roots descend; each star passes between backing and moon-skin bridge at the closed endpoint.

motion_and_geometry.degrees_of_freedom: One intended operating degree of freedom. The left wing's integral shoe rotates its root; equal complete external gears constrain the right wing to the opposite angle. Chassis operating pockets suppress translation and axial lift after assembly.
motion_and_geometry.travel: Each wing rotates 82 degrees. With the thumb-shoe path at 15 mm radius, nominal arc travel is 15 * radians(82) = 21.5 mm.
states_to_check: 0 degrees closed: both stop shoulders seated; wing edges within chassis silhouette; all six stars lie over solid backing and beneath moon-skin bridges.
20 degrees: leading tips clear the chassis rim and root guards.
41 degrees: primary intermediate inspection for bridge release, trailing-edge clearance, and pinch access.
62 degrees: aperture ligaments and thumb arm clear the opposite gear guard.
82 degrees open: both open stops seated without tooth-end contact; deployed silhouette is mirror-symmetric about X.
motion_and_geometry.hard_stops: Broad 4.8 by 6 mm wing-root shoulders contact replaceable-looking but integral chassis lands at closed and open endpoints. The complete root gears retain continuous engagement; teeth never serve as travel stops.

concept.z_stack_and_assembly: Z=0 is the chassis back face. The chassis backing occupies Z=0-4.0 mm. Both coplanar wing webs and both complete root gears occupy Z=4.5-7.5 mm in operation, leaving 0.50 mm below. Gear-guard, entry-lip, and moon-skin-bridge undersides are at Z=8.0 mm and their roofs end by Z=10.4 mm, leaving 0.50 mm above; the 11.0 mm envelope includes surface relief. Each journal's mushroom-flange underside is at Z=9.2 mm and its top at Z=10.4 mm. For assembly only, the open roof gates at -118/+118 degrees admit the two roots sequentially onto Z=5.7-8.7 mm service shelves, 1.2 mm above the operating plane and still 0.50 mm below the flange underside, where their stop lugs pass over the operating bosses. Load the right wing at -118 degrees and leave it raised; load the left at +118 degrees and leave it raised; mesh the two complete gears at the engraved service timing marks; then counter-rotate both together from +/-118 degrees to 0 while raised. At zero, aligned shelf drop windows allow both roots to descend together 1.2 mm into the operating pockets. The operating roof, mushroom flanges, and guide cheeks then limit axial play to 0.45 mm and prevent either root from rising over a stop or translating to a service lobe. The 0-82-degree stops keep the seated roots at least 30 degrees from a roof gate. Verify simultaneous seating and both closed stop contacts before cycling. No glue, pin, screw, magnet, string, support removal, forced flex, or snap is part of assembly.
concept.print_stance: Chassis prints broad smooth back on the bed; every retaining lip uses a 45-degree tent profile and no horizontal roof span above 4 mm. Each wing prints flat on its inner face with the journal axis vertical, through-stars vertical, pad face upward, and vein ribs upward. All three stances are intended support-free for a 0.4 mm nozzle process, subject to slicer inspection in Make.
distinctive_features: A calm crescent pebble silhouette expands to roughly three times its closed width.
Six tiny five-point openings appear only as true negative space once they leave their fixed moon-skin bridges and backing.
The broad moon-notch pad follows the crescent instead of adding a protruding knob.
Two equal root gears make the bilateral cooperation visible through one guarded inspection window.
The chassis backing shows a small raised constellation after deployment, echoing the apertures without relying on color.
concept.safety_strategy: No stored-energy element or forced flexure is intended. The lower 24 mm grip island stays at least 15 mm from either swept wing edge. Root gears, bayonet gates, and counter-rotating shear lines sit under 2.4 mm-thick roofs extending at least 12 mm radially from each pivot. At each body-side wing entrance, an 8 mm-long overlapping lip holds its underside at Z=8.0 mm over the 3.0 mm wing, creating only the specified 0.50 mm roof gap; in the last 18 degrees of closing the moving trailing edge is already at least 5 mm under this lip. Outside the guarded entrances, the nearest opposed moving/fixed edges remain at least 6 mm apart until they pass under the lip. The thumb shoe stays above the wing plane inside a 2.0 mm raised rim with a 0.8 mm planar slot gap and no exposed undercut. Make must enforce these dimensions through the whole sweep with a conservative fingertip probe and avoid any claim of certified child safety without physical review.
assumptions: The request's 'slider' accepts a broad control that translates along an arcuate guide while remaining integral to one wing; this is a deliberate three-part resolution, not a fourth prismatic body.
A common 0.4 mm-nozzle FDM printer and one rigid filament are the production baseline; exact material, shrink, friction, and surface finish remain Make/Release choices.
Nominal clearances are diameter-independent design gaps, to be parameterized and checked rather than treated as universal printer capability.
The open product is a desk-scale handled object, not a toy certified for a specific age group.
unresolved_risks: The raised-service-plane bayonet sequence is specified kinematically but not yet built; Make must prove sequential loading, simultaneous gear timing and pocket drop, axial retention, and that tolerance accumulation cannot reopen a release path.
Gear backlash that prints freely may create visible endpoint timing error; Make must tune gear center distance and stop timing with a clearance coupon or controlled parameter study.

The fixed moon-skin bridges conceal the apertures but introduce local seams and roof spans; product-derived close views and slices must confirm the pebble reads smooth and the bridges remain support-free.
No physical cycle, friction, wear, jam, pinch, print, or first-use discovery evidence exists at Invent; these must not be claimed from the concept alone.
The 136 mm open width is desk-scale but wider than the closed palm form; Make must confirm the exact swept envelope and stability when placed on a desk.

research.scope: Source-backed FDM starting points plus explicit design calculations. Sources support general modeling choices only; they do not prove this mechanism, printer fit, safety, or physical performance.

sources.title: Modeling with 3D printing in mind
sources.supported_claims: FFF layers need support beneath them; short bridges can print, ordinary support-free overhang guidance is roughly 45-60 degrees, a common nozzle is 0.4 mm, no fit tolerance is universal, and at least 0.3 mm is presented as an initial moving-part value.
sources.application: Use flat wing stances, 45-degree tented chassis lips, structural features many nozzle widths thick, and an adjustable 0.50 mm moving-clearance baseline. Require slicer and exact-CAD checks rather than treating the guideline as proof.

sources.title: SolidWorks Tutorial: Modeling and Inspection Masterclass for 3D Printing
sources.supported_claims: The article presents 1.2 mm as a good FDM minimum-wall starting point for a typical 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.5 mm spacing for separated parts, and 45-degree FDM support-free overhang guidance.
sources.application: Set substantially thicker 2.4-6.0 mm load paths, 0.50 mm initial moving gaps, and 45-degree support-facing chamfers. These are conservative design decisions, not certified limits.

design_calculations: Equal external gears at equal center distance impose equal-magnitude opposite angular motion; this geometric relation motivates the 1:1 bilateral drive.
Nominal thumb travel is arc length r*theta = 15 mm * (82*pi/180) = 21.5 mm.

Nominal deployed half-span from a 58 mm pivot-to-tip reach at 82 degrees is about 57.4 mm transverse; two half-spans plus two 9 mm pivot offsets total 132.8 mm, so the sealed 136 mm width adds 3.2 mm margin.

alternatives_considered.family: Central translating dual-cam slider plus two mutually hinged wing shells
alternatives_considered.advantage: Literal straight slider and visually pure symmetry.
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: With exactly three physical parts there is no independent frame; the mutual hinge, linear guide, axial capture, and fixed reference collapse into a difficult stacked interlock with a higher assembly and jam risk.

alternatives_considered.family: Central wedge slider spreading two wing-shell halves
alternatives_considered.advantage: Very few fine features and a broad push surface.
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: A wedge positively opens but does not positively synchronize the return path, and its behavior depends too much on grip friction and shell squeeze.

alternatives_considered.family: Twin geared roots with integral arcuate slider
alternatives_considered.advantage: Exactly three physical parts, stable chassis reference, direct 1:1 counter-rotation, positive opening and closing, and inspectable stops.
alternatives_considered.selection_reason: Best combined compliance with the part count, one obvious reversible motion, symmetric unfurling, support-free part stances, and robust rigid-body construction.

verification_required_in_make: Create source-first parametric CAD with exactly three product parts and explicit closed/intermediate/open configurations.

Check mesh/solid validity, part count, the complete Z stack, wall and ligament thickness, gear contact across the stroke, hard-stop timing, five-pose collision, 0.80 mm nonmeshing planar gaps, and 0.50 mm roof gaps.
Demonstrate sequential loading in the raised service plane, simultaneous geared rotation and pocket drop, and verify the seated operating arc cannot rise over a stop or reach either bayonet gate.
Slice each declared stance with supports disabled and preserve orientation evidence; do not equate a slicer preview with a successful print.
Render closed, 41-degree, open, raised-service assembly, seated assembly, and exploded states from exact geometry; inspect bridge release, entry-lip overlap, star masking, and the closed pebble read.
Keep physical fit, feel, wear, cycle life, and human discovery explicitly unverified until corresponding real evidence exists.
